skill_score.definition: skill = 1 - MAE_model / MAE_seasonal_naive, both measured on the same untouched hold-out. Positive skill means the model genuinely improves on 'same hour last week'. This is reported alongside MASE because MASE's denominator is in-sample error, so MASE < 1 alone is not proof of skill.

conformal.guarantee: Coverage is at least 80% under exchangeability of the calibration and test sets, with no assumption about the model or the noise distribution.
conformal.caveat: For time series, exchangeability is approximate: the calibration block is the most recent data before the test period, so a drifting process weakens the guarantee. Empirical coverage is therefore measured on the test set and reported against nominal rather than assumed.

interval.calibration_effect: Raw quantile band covered 67.1% (width 88.7); after conformal calibration it covers 79.2% (width 103.5). The price of honest coverage is a wider band, and that is the correct trade.

split.rationale: The target is a time series, so the only honest evaluation is out-of-sample in the future. Train covers 2011-01-08 00:00:00 to 2012-08-09 04:00:00; test covers 2012-08-09 05:00:00 onward. No shuffling at any point.

cv_protocol.rationale: Expanding-window folds keep training strictly in the past. The purge drops the 168 rows before each validation fold so trailing-window features cannot span the boundary, and the embargo skips the first 24 validation rows to break autocorrelation carry-over.

leaderboard.assumption: Demand depends non-linearly on hour, weather and recent history, with interactions -- e.g. rain matters far more at commuting hours than at 3am.
Demand is a linear combination of its own past and calendar effects. Fast, transparent, and a fair test of whether non-linearity is needed at all.
Demand this hour equals demand the same hour last week. No parameters, no fitting -- the baseline MASE is defined against it.

horizons.method: At horizon h, every lag shorter than h is removed, because it would not have been observed yet. This is the difference between a real multi-step forecast and a one-step model evaluated dishonestly.
horizons.interpretation: Error grows from MAE 28.797 at 1 hour to 53.446 at 168 hours as recent history falls away and only calendar and weather remain.

baselines.description: Predict this hour equals last hour.

baselines.description: Same hour last week -- the MASE denominator.
